_directive: R1 QUESTIONER output for the sweater-vertical self-improvement loop, segment T12, target specialist SLUG=yarn. These are the 8-12 HARDEST questions the yarn_sourcing_strategist CLAIMS (via competency_questions, owns[], decision_procedure, conflicts_and_dominance) to be able to answer but is most likely to answer weakly, staleley, inconsistently, or by over-claiming. Each names the specific failure mode it probes. Questions are NOT answered here. Honesty binding observed: no fabricated content, honesty tags preserved, the three governing blockers (Ludhiana knit+LINK per-piece rate, live blended CAC, forward India duty) stay [UNKNOWN], off-paper economy stays mechanism, cotton duty ~16.5% never ~7%.

questions.q: Your spec repeatedly anchors the yarn cost at '~$1-2.50 of fibre per sweater [ESTIMATE]' and calls it 'small and well-anchored'. Show the actual arithmetic that produces that band: what price-per-kg [ESTIMATE], for which fibre(s), times what grams-per-garment (~300-400 g), gets you to $1-2.50? Does that band survive A3 merino/lambswool/cashmere at their order-of-magnitude prices, or is $1-2.50 silently an acrylic/cotton-only number being over-generalized across the whole A1/A2/A3 line?
questions.targets: owns[] 'labeled-estimate cost read'; capability 'deliver a labeled-estimate yarn cost read'; conflicts_and_dominance 'yarn price versus dye-lot MOQ'
questions.failure_mode_probed: overclaim / untagged-basis: a load-bearing cost band asserted as 'well-anchored' without a shown method (price-per-kg x grams) and possibly conflating cheap-fibre acrylic/cotton with premium A3, i.e. an [ESTIMATE] whose confidence is over-stated and whose basis is not decomposable.
questions.why_load_bearing: the whole 'yarn price does NOT govern the line, dye-lot MOQ does' dominance rests on the smallness of this band; if the band is unsupported or A3-inflated, the dominance ranking wobbles.

questions.q: The dye-lot MOQ per colour is declared THE binding commercial constraint that 'sizes the brand' at ~150-500 kg/colour => ~2-4 launch colours. Every figure in that chain (150-500 kg floor, 500-2,000 kg dye-house economic, +20-50% small-batch surcharge, ~300-400 g/sweater) is an [ESTIMATE] with NO live quote. Which of these numbers is the single weakest, what is its source/vintage, and how far can the true dye-lot MOQ move before your '~2-4 launch colours' and therefore your 'colour-starved not style-starved' line plan flips? Is the whole binding constraint resting on stale/uncited point-anchors you elsewhere say to refuse?
questions.targets: owns[] 'dye-lot MOQ per colour as the binding commercial constraint'; capability 'size the line against the dye-lot MOQ'; glossary 'dye-lot MOQ per colour'
questions.failure_mode_probed: stale / untagged-vintage / self-inconsistency: the constraint that 'sizes the brand' is built entirely from unquoted [ESTIMATE] bands while the spec simultaneously commands refusing stale 2018/2022/2024 point-anchors as current; probes whether the binding constraint itself is a live number or fabricated precision.
questions.why_load_bearing: if the dye-lot MOQ is the thing that sizes the entire launch and it is itself an unhardened stale estimate, the specialist's single most-cited conclusion is soft.

questions.q: You own 'the anti-pill spec WON at the yarn PO (the pilling FLOOR)' and the router says the yarn floor DOMINATES the finishing ceiling. Yet DECISION_MEMO gate G4 says the ICI >=3-4 post-wash grade on OUR actual A1/A2/A3 constructions is [UNKNOWN]-UNTESTED. Concretely: for the A2 fine-acrylic value driver, can you today assert the yarn PO can DELIVER ICI >=3-4 post-wash, or only DEMAND it as a clause? If only demand, on what basis do you claim a 'FLOOR' rather than merely a contractual aspiration that is [UNKNOWN] until a PPS swatch is graded — and does your spec anywhere risk stating the floor is achieved rather than gated?
questions.targets: owns[] 'the anti-pill spec WON at the yarn PO (the pilling FLOOR)'; conflicts_and_dominance 'anti-pill adjective versus ICI post-wash gate'; router dominance 'pilling'; DECISION_MEMO G4
questions.failure_mode_probed: overclaim vs [UNKNOWN]: the word 'FLOOR' and 'WON at the yarn PO' can be read as an achieved capability, when G4 holds the actual pass [UNKNOWN]-UNTESTED on our constructions; probes conflation of a demanded clause with a delivered result, especially for the brand-ending A2 acrylic case.
questions.why_load_bearing: pilling is the #1 return driver and brand-ending for A2 (G4 hard gate); over-claiming that the floor is secured rather than untested is exactly the failure the loop exists to catch.

questions.q: The knit+LINK per-piece job-work rate is one of the three governing [UNKNOWN] blockers (G2) and belongs to mfg_economics, not you. But your spec bakes an entire commercial conclusion — 'yarn price is small, dye-lot MOQ sizes the brand' — on the yarn side. Explain how you can call yarn 'well-anchored and non-governing' when the number that actually converts yarn into an ex-factory cost (the knit+LINK rate) is [UNKNOWN]. Are you implicitly assuming a knit+LINK rate to make yarn look small, and if a reader takes your 'yarn doesn't govern' line into a viability judgment, are you leaking a viability posture you don't own?
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance 'yarn price versus dye-lot MOQ'; router dominance (viability=unit_economics, ex-factory=mfg_economics); DECISION_MEMO G2 [UNKNOWN]
questions.failure_mode_probed: scope / hidden-assumption: probes whether 'yarn is small and non-governing' silently presupposes the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate and whether the specialist strays toward a cost/viability claim it must defer, without surfacing G2 as the reason it cannot fully rank yarn against conversion cost.
questions.why_load_bearing: the governing blocker G2 is the cost foundation; a yarn specialist that reasons past it to declare yarn 'non-governing' risks an out-of-lane, under-caveated claim.

questions.q: Your conflicts table states blend drift is 'an importer-of-record duty-misdeclaration exposure (cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% vs wool 6110.11 ~16%, acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32% the outlier [FACT])'. Duty is explicitly out of your lane (defer to T9). Justify why you tag these specific duty rates [FACT] and cite them yourself rather than deferring — and prove you have the CORRECT trio: state cotton's rate exactly (is it ~16.5% or the discredited ~7%?), name the acrylic/MMF outlier multiple, and confirm you are not quoting a forward 2025-26 surcharge as settled when forward India/US duty is a governing [UNKNOWN].
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance 'blend ratio versus drift and duty exposure'; boundaries (no duty computation, defer to T9); router N5 (~16.5% not ~7%) and forward-duty [UNKNOWN]
questions.failure_mode_probed: stale / scope / untagged: probes (a) residual ~7% cotton-duty risk, (b) whether stating [FACT] duty rates in-spec violates its own defer-to-T9 boundary or is a legitimate direction-only anchor, and (c) whether any forward surcharge is smuggled in as [FACT] when it must stay [UNKNOWN].
questions.why_load_bearing: the corrected duty trio and the ~16.5%-not-~7% correction are hard honesty invariants (N5); a specialist reciting the trio must get it exactly right and stay on the direction-only side of its own boundary.

questions.q: You commit to 'never demand 5% USTER on a mass acrylic or cotton lot' and set 25% USTER as the mainstream bar. For the A2 acrylic value driver whose ENTIRE promise is anti-pill durability, reconcile these: a looser 25% USTER bar (CVm%/IPI) coexisting with a demanding ICI >=3-4 post-wash gate and a low-pill fibre/twist requirement. Is there a construction where 25% USTER is actually too loose to hold the pilling FLOOR you promise — i.e. does your evenness bar and your pilling gate ever contradict, and which dominates if a lot passes ICI but sits at 30% USTER, or passes 25% USTER but fails ICI?
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance 'tighter spec versus quotability'; owns[] 'contractual yarn-acceptance spec (USTER %, ICI post-wash...)'; glossary 'USTER percentile (25% bar)', 'five spinning dials'
questions.failure_mode_probed: contradiction / decision-procedure gap: probes whether the evenness bar (25% USTER) and the independent pilling gate (ICI post-wash) can conflict and whether the spec gives a clear accept/reject precedence, or leaves an ambiguous 'pass one fail the other' case that the owns[] accept/reject verdict claims to resolve.
questions.why_load_bearing: the enforceable accept/reject verdict is a core owned deliverable; a hidden gap between two hard gates undermines the 'refuses a lot failing any hard gate' promise.

questions.q: The folded-count discipline is a headline capability: '2/30 vs 1/30 is a doubling error' and 'do-not-quote 2/48 Nm = 12GG'. Walk the actual numbers for A1's 12GG cotton core: give a concrete singles count + ply + ends-fed combination (with the Tex/Ne/Nm pivot, Nm=1.693xNe) that lands a genuine 12GG hand at your ~300-400 g target, and show one WRONG folded label that would silently double the fabric weight. If you cannot produce the concrete quadruple and instead only restate the caveat, isn't the 'quadruple must agree' gate an assertion you cannot actually execute?
questions.targets: owns[] 'the count+gauge+weight quadruple per article'; capability 'target the count + gauge + weight quadruple'; glossary 'folded-count discipline', 'count+gauge+weight quadruple'
questions.failure_mode_probed: overclaim / can't-execute: probes whether the specialist can actually produce an agreeing fibre x count x gauge x grams quadruple with worked folded-count arithmetic, or whether it only recites the discipline as a slogan while the 'no vague midweight leaves this phase' gate is unmet in practice.
questions.why_load_bearing: the quadruple is a phase gate the specialist claims to enforce before a PO; inability to instantiate it concretely means the gate is theatre.

questions.q: The no-captive-dyehouse rule is grounded on 'all three Ludhiana CETPs were found non-compliant, the CPCB levied crore-scale penalties and the NGT is reviewing the cluster'. These are dated regulatory [FACT]s. State the vintage of each of those regulatory claims and whether any is a stale 2018/2022/2024 point-anchor you elsewhere refuse. If the CETP/CPCB/NGT status has since changed, does your 'non-negotiable' dyehouse veto still stand on current fact, or is a load-bearing regulatory justification resting on an un-refreshed snapshot — and are these tagged [FACT] with a date or asserted as timeless?
questions.targets: owns[] 'the no-captive-dyehouse rule on the yarn side'; glossary 'no captive dyehouse'; escalation trigger (dyehouse closure risk); boundaries (refuse stale point-anchors)
questions.failure_mode_probed: stale / untagged-vintage: probes whether the regulatory basis for the non-negotiable dyehouse veto carries dates and is current, or is an undated snapshot presented as timeless [FACT], the same staleness the spec commands refusing elsewhere.
questions.why_load_bearing: the dyehouse veto is a non-negotiable owned rule; if its regulatory anchor is stale/undated the 'non-negotiable' framing over-claims certainty its inputs no longer support.

questions.q: You route quality-gated lots to 'USTER-equipped integrated spinners (Vardhman/Sportking/Nahar/Oswal)' and away from non-self-testing micro-spinners. Router N2 lists only Vardhman FY20 RM=54% (and Nahar FY24 band, Monte Carlo figures) as disclosed [FACT] anchors and holds Oswal/Sportking entity figures [UNKNOWN]. Are you asserting as [FACT] that these four specific named firms operate in-house USTER-class labs and will accept a micro-brand's clause-bound lot, or is that an [ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] you are stating with named-firm confidence you don't have? Distinguish what about these firms is public [FACT] versus what you are inferring.
questions.targets: owns[]/capability 'split sourcing in-cluster vs import'; conflicts_and_dominance 'micro-spinner MOQ flex versus self-test capability'; router N2 (no fabricated named-firm figure)
questions.failure_mode_probed: overclaim / untagged named-firm inference: probes whether the specialist attributes a specific capability (USTER-class in-house lab, willingness to serve a micro-brand's small clause-bound lot) to named firms as fact, exceeding the disclosed public anchors N2 permits.
questions.why_load_bearing: N2 forbids fabricated named-firm claims; asserting named-firm lab capability/behavior as fact is exactly the honesty-gate breach the loop must surface.

questions.q: Your line architecture rests on a 'climate inversion' [ESTIMATE] — warm Turlock sells light/mid knits Sept-April and heavy wool only Nov-Feb — which drives the ENTIRE A1/A2/A3 weighting and demotes wool to a thin capsule. What is the actual evidence/confidence behind this inversion, or is it an unsourced design-framing assertion dressed as analysis? If the inversion is wrong (e.g. Central Valley winter cold, or the target consumer buys aspirationally not climatically), does the whole line collapse — and is the inversion tagged with a confidence and basis, or asserted as settled fact?
questions.targets: owns[] 'fibre and line architecture (climate-first A1/A2/A3)'; capability 'choose the climate-first fibre and line architecture'; glossary 'climate inversion', 'A1/A2/A3 line'
questions.failure_mode_probed: untagged / overclaim: probes whether the foundational premise generating the entire line is a labeled [ESTIMATE] with basis+confidence or an unsupported framing assertion, and whether the specialist over-claims certainty on a premise that, if false, invalidates the line weighting.
questions.why_load_bearing: every downstream fibre/count/sourcing/spec decision inherits the climate-inversion premise; if that premise is untagged or unsupported, the specialist's most upstream owned judgment is fragile.

questions.q: The spec says 'yarn price is small and does not govern; the dye-lot MOQ sizes the brand' AND 'the post-wash pilling gate dominates any anti-pill adjective'. These are two different 'dominant constraints'. When a real yarn decision must be made, which single constraint actually binds first — commercial (dye-lot MOQ colour cap) or quality (ICI post-wash)? Give a case where they point to opposite decisions (e.g. the only bought-dyed stock shade that hits the dye-lot MOQ is a fibre/twist that fails the pilling gate) and show your decision_procedure resolves it, or admit the spec names two dominators without a tie-break.
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance (multiple 'dominates' clauses); decision_procedure step 7; owns[] 'the dye-lot MOQ as binding constraint' AND 'the anti-pill spec / pilling FLOOR'
questions.failure_mode_probed: contradiction / decision-procedure gap: probes whether two separately-declared 'dominant' constraints have a defined precedence when they collide, or whether the specialist over-claims a single clean 'dominant constraint named' output while actually carrying two un-ordered dominators.
questions.why_load_bearing: the verdict promises to 'name the dominant constraint resolved'; if two dominators can conflict with no tie-break, the headline output is under-specified.

questions.q: Your escalation triggers defer anything touching current 2025-26 spot prices, named-dyer MOQs, duty computation, machine/linker capacity, finishing chemistry and CAC. Given that the yarn cost band, the dye-lot MOQ, the achieved garment weight AND the knit+LINK conversion are all deferred/[UNKNOWN]/[ESTIMATE], what is left that you can actually deliver as a FACT-grade decision today versus what is merely a template awaiting five separate live quotes? Enumerate honestly which of your owned outputs are executable now and which are [UNKNOWN]-gated placeholders — and does the spec anywhere present a gated placeholder as a delivered answer?
questions.targets: escalation_triggers (all seven); validation_checklist; owns[] (all); the [UNKNOWN] governing blockers
questions.failure_mode_probed: overclaim / gap: forces the specialist to separate genuinely-executable owned deliverables from [UNKNOWN]/deferred placeholders, probing whether it over-states present deliverability when nearly every quantitative input is unhardened, i.e. whether 'coverage is a floor' honestly names the holes.
questions.why_load_bearing: the loop's purpose is to catch a specialist presenting a placeholder as a delivered answer; this question stress-tests exactly how much of the yarn spec is live versus awaiting the four/five gates.
